G-1010 Performance-Based Compensation For Teachers And Administrators 
 
The District shall implement and maintain a method of compensation for its 
teachers and school administrators that includes job performance and job 
accomplishments as a significant factor in determining compensation and 
additional compensation. 
 
The assessment of job performance shall incorporate a rigorous, transparent, and 
fair evaluation system that evaluates a teacher’s or school administrator’s 
performance at least in part based upon data  on student growth as measured by 
assessments and other objective criteria. 
 
Decisions about the development, content, standards, procedures, adoption and 
implementation of the method of compensation required under section 1250 of 
the Michigan Revised School Code, decisions about how an employee 
performance evaluation system is used to determine performance -based 
compensation under section 1250, and decisions concerning the performance -
based compensation of an individual employee, or the impact of those  decisions 
on an individual employee or the bargaining unit, are within the sole authority of 
the public school employer to decide and shall not be the subject of any terms and 
conditions within a collective bargaining agreement between the District and a 
collective bargaining representative of such teachers.  
 
With the exception of the performance-based compensation for the Superintendent, 
the Board of Education delegates to the Superintendent or designee(s), the 
responsibility for taking appropriate action, including developing administrative 
guidelines as needed, to implement and maintain a method of compensation that 
includes job performance and job accomplishments as a significant factor in 
accordance with Section 1250. 
 
References: MCL 380.1250, effective July 19, 2011; MCL 423.215. 
 
Adopted: June 18, 2013

LETTER OF AGREEMENT 
between 
The Troy School District 
and the 
Troy Education Association, MEA/NEA 
regarding 
Schoology Online Grading and Communication 
  
 
The Parties have previously negotiated contract language and letters of agreement regarding 
notification of academic progress through formal progress reports, report card grades, and semester 
grades in Sections 14.14 and 14.15 of the 2017-2020 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA).  This 
letter of agreement shall amend those sections only through June 16, 2020. 
 
This letter of agreement references the use of Schoology as a tool for reporting academic progress and 
communicating information for students/parents. 
 
1. Secondary teachers shall report student academic progress via Schoology. 
2. At a minimum, teachers will post their course syllabus/expectations including course outline, 
grading policies, and major assignment due dates (any assignment reasonably predicte d to 
consist of more than 15% of a student’s marking period grade) on Schoology. 
3. Teachers will maintain and update grades on Schoology so that the grades will be current
 
within 2 school days following the conclusion of approximately the 3rd, 6th and 10th week of each 
card marking (timeline provided below). 
4. The Schoology report shall contain all relevant information so that students/parents will have 
access to the student’s current overall grade and the grade for each assignment that counts 
towards the student's current grade for the course. 
5. Also, teachers will use Schoology for one-way student-to-student communication and teacher-to-
student communication as a way of keeping students and parents informed about major, 
significant events specifically related to the course.   
6. Teachers are encouraged but not required to share resources with colleagues using the 
collaborative, digital space within Schoology. 
7. If a student has been identified by the school psychologist, social worker, counselor or 
administrator as needing special attention and progress monitoring, arrangements can be made 
to provide more frequent progress reports for those students as provided for in Article 14.15.  
8. Furthermore, it is recognized that grades may be required for certain students earlie r than the 
time lines above, and the teachers agree to cooperate and submit grades earlier under these 
special circumstances (examples of special circumstances include student moving, scholarship 
consideration, and admission to college). 
9. The District shall provide on-going professional development specific to Schoology, as may be 
necessary and/or upon reasonable request. 
10. The parties agree to bargain changes to working conditions in regard to future usage of 
Schoology for purposes related to grade reporting and student/parent communication during 
negotiations for the successor agreement to the current CBA.

7. B.  PERSONNEL 
 
CONSIDERATION:  Administrative Appointment –  
     Assistant Principal, Larson Middle School 
 
I am pleased to recommend the appointment of Mr. David Recker to the position 
of Assistant Principal, Larson Middle School .   Mr. Recker started his career in 
education following graduation from college in 2012.  He began his education 
career teaching Language Arts and Journalism in Dayton, Ohio at the Dayton 
Early College Academy.  Mr. Recker then moved to the Troy area in 2014 and 
accepted a Language Arts teaching position at Troy High School.  During his time 
in Dayton and at Troy High School, he fulfilled many additional responsibilities 
including implementing the International Society for Technology in Education’s 
standards, leading the Continuous Improvement Committee to increase use of 
best practices and served as coordinator for several extracurricular clubs and 
committees.   Mr. Recker has a Bachelor’s Degree in Adolescent to Young Adult 
Education from the University of Da yton and a Master of Arts in K-12 Education 
Administration from Michigan State University.   
 
With your approval, Mr. Recker will begin his duties as Assistant Principal, Larson 
Middle School as of July 1, 2017.

struggling students, I am always attempting to contribute to society in a positive manner. This personal quality rubs off on my students, 
and I believe it makes me a strong candidate for this position. 
My professional experiences have prepared me for this position as well. For the first two years of my career, I worked tirelessly at an 
urban, early college high school. I learned how to manage, motivate, and teach students of all ability levels without sacrificing rigor. I 
also advised sixteen students and developed positive relationships with countless others. Due to this, I earned the highest possible 
value-added score as measured by the Ohio Department of Education.  
For the past three years, I have taught various levels of English classes at Troy High School--from remedial 9th grade to 12 AP. 
Additionally, I have led adult learning as the school improvement chair at Troy High School and as a teacher leader for the Troy School 
District. Furthermore, I interned for over 220 hours with Remo Roncone, principal of Troy High School, while completing a M.A. in 
K-12 Educational Administration at Michigan State University. I believe that these professional experiences will allow me to become a 
valuable member of your schoolÃ¢â¬â¢s community and culture.  
Statement  
ADM1. What personal characteristics define an excellent administrator?  
It is the fundamental responsibility of an excellent administrator to maintain a physically safe environment for students, teachers, and 
school personnel to interact in. In addition to ensuring the safety of the school community, they must work creatively with school 
resources and community partners to meet the physiological needs of the students. These essential necessities of students must be met 
before any sense of community or upper-level learning can occur within the school. 
Once the physical environment of the school is maintained and the physiological needs of the students are satisfied, a skilled 
administrator will gather the resources teachers need to achieve impressive instructional outcomes. These resources must also be utilized

to achieve a shared school vision. Additionally, it is imperative that they be distributed ethically among all subgroups of students so that 
all students may be provided with an equitable education. 
Besides just providing teachers with physical resources for classroom instruction, it is also critical that excellent administrators serve as 
instructional leaders for the staff. Doing so means that they must remain current on best teaching practices and use instructional rounds 
for the sake of teacher improvement rather than just evaluation. By spending time focused on cultivating rigorous and coherent 
instruction as well as modeling the behaviors expected of the teaching staff, an exemplary administrator will cultivate a professional and 
capable learning community. 
Also, it is essential that an excellent administrator fosters a positive school culture. Students of all ability levels must perceive that they 
belong to this school community while still being encouraged to exhibit growth in their academic achievement. Such a school culture 
will engage parents and guardians to help encourage student success. Student success will be defined by both progress and achievement 
on standardized assessments as well as by studentsÃ¢â¬â¢ abilities to think creatively, act ethically, and respond to challenges with resiliency. 
Furthermore, it is crucial that an excellent administrator act as a bridge for students, families, and teachers to work collaboratively for 
the best interests of students. The best interests of students must be at the heart of all school decisions while still showing respect for the 
time, effort, and professional experiences of teachers. It is important to note that doing what is in the best interests of students does not 
always mean that they will be given superfluous circumstances; instead, at times it may be necessary to allow students to experience 
failure so that they may learn from their mistakes and succeed in the future beyond the secondary classroom. 
Finally, administrators must remain cognizant of the symbolism of their actions, statements, and time. These three domains will 
symbolize what the school values. As a result, they should all communicate integrity toward achieving the schoolÃ¢â¬â¢s mission. By 
distributing leadership, maintaining professional learning committees, and implementing systems-level structures, model administrators 
will symbolize the sustainable collaboration necessary for the school to succeed as well. Ultimately, school leaders must remember to be 
the creative, ethical, and resilient individuals that they want their students to become.   
ADM2. From your point of view, how important is technology in education. What technology-related skills can you 
contribute to a school district?  
From my point of view, technology is essential for educating students in the 21st century. Students must be able to use technology 
efficiently and responsibly. Likewise, teachers must be able to facilitate this process in order to reach contemporary students. 
I possess the ability to help a school use technology for the sake of enhancing instruction, assessment, and communication. For example, 
I can help teachers learn how to channel student voice through the creation of podcasts and iMovie trailers. Additionally, I can lead 
professional learning on assessment with electronic rubrics and voice feedback to make growth more accessible for students. Finally, I 
am able to effectively use email and social media for community engagement. I believe that I would be able to help a school 
troubleshoot most technology-related scenarios.

Growth, Equity and Accountability, along with  members of the Teaching &

13th Board Workshop.  The total cost of these materials is $419,606.82.  At this

questions and concerns. We are planning on doing the same if we are successful in acquiring this new 
property, which we are proposing to call “Whispering Park”.
 
Again, our plan intends to preserve acres of existing trees and assumes that we will work closely with 
the surrounding community, strategically placing the new homes while also re-planting new  
trees. We estimate that we will be able to preserve more than 20% of the total acreage for Whispering 
Park. 
“Whispering Park” will be attracting young homebuyer families who are often reaching out to us, due 
to our strong reputation as well as the strong reputation of the Troy School District. This group of 
young families brings many benefits to the Troy School district as they want their children to start from 
K through 12.  
 
Sincere thanks in advance for your careful consideration of our proposal, which follows. Again, we would 
consider ourselves fortunate to earn the selection by the Troy School District for this important project 
and our team would look very much forward to engaging with yours, as appropriate, to ensure the 
enduring success of Whispering Park.

450
TO
: Board of Education  
 
FROM: Rick West, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services
CC: Dr. Richard Machesky, Superintendent  
RE: S ervice Contract Renewals 
  
DATE: Thursday, June 8, 2017  
The initial terms for three of our service cont racts expire on June 30, 2017 and we have been in 
negotiations with our providers regarding renewal terms of e ach of the contracts.  Following is a 
summary of the contracts and recommendations for each:  
First Student – First Student provides bus transportation services for our school district.  The initial 
term of our contract was for the three-year period commencing July 1, 2014 and ending June 30, 2017. 
There is an option to extend the contract (Renewal Term) for up to two additional years.  Currently, we 
have a very competitive contract based on per route pricing and believe we can negotiate a better deal 
for a two-year renewal than if we were to bid the services. 
Recommendation:  We have been negotiating pricing for a two-year renewal with First Student.  Given 
our competitive per route cost, the starting wage for bus drivers is low relative to neighboring districts. 
This is causing difficulty in staffing; therefore, we will be recommending a renewal contract that will 
increase the per route cost by 5% - 8% for the first year and 3% - 5% for the second year.  Again, given 
some comparative data on per route cost of other school districts in the county and the nation-wide bus 
driver shortage, we believe we will be better served by negotiating a renewal around those parameters. 
This increase will be reflected in the 2017-18 proposed budget. 
Safe Ed – Safe Ed provides professional security consultation solutions at Troy Athens, Troy High 
School, and Troy Career and College High School.  The initial term of our contract was for the three-
year period commencing July 1, 2014 and ending June 30, 2017.

RE: S ervice Contract Renewals 
  
DATE: Thursday, June 8, 2017  
The initial terms for three of our service cont racts expire on June 30, 2017 and we have been in 
negotiations with our providers regarding renewal terms of e ach of the contracts.  Following is a 
summary of the contracts and recommendations for each:  
First Student – First Student provides bus transportation services for our school district.  The initial 
term of our contract was for the three-year period commencing July 1, 2014 and ending June 30, 2017. 
There is an option to extend the contract (Renewal Term) for up to two additional years.  Currently, we 
have a very competitive contract based on per route pricing and believe we can negotiate a better deal 
for a two-year renewal than if we were to bid the services. 
Recommendation:  We have been negotiating pricing for a two-year renewal with First Student.  Given 
our competitive per route cost, the starting wage for bus drivers is low relative to neighboring districts. 
This is causing difficulty in staffing; therefore, we will be recommending a renewal contract that will 
increase the per route cost by 5% - 8% for the first year and 3% - 5% for the second year.  Again, given 
some comparative data on per route cost of other school districts in the county and the nation-wide bus 
driver shortage, we believe we will be better served by negotiating a renewal around those parameters. 
This increase will be reflected in the 2017-18 proposed budget. 
Safe Ed – Safe Ed provides professional security consultation solutions at Troy Athens, Troy High 
School, and Troy Career and College High School.  The initial term of our contract was for the three-
year period commencing July 1, 2014 and ending June 30, 2017.  
Recommendation: Safe Ed has been a quality partner in providing security  services for us since 2011. 
We recommend entering into a succe ssor agreement for three years  commencing July 1, 2017 and 
ending on June 30, 2020.  Our current base contract cost is $300,500 and it is recommended the base 
contract for the three years be as follows:  $305,000; $310,000; and $315,000; respectively.

full coverage insurance.  I am recommending that we make this change which will provide us a more 
predictable budget number for workers compensation and eliminates the $400,000 exposure per 
employee injury.

2017 Sinking Fund Community Input Survey Report 2
471
Survey Background
• Because of persistent funding gaps from the State, the Troy School District continues to seek 
other ways fund quality education in the District.  
• In 2013 voters overwhelmingly supported the District’s request for a 125 million dollar bond to 
help cover many expenses over the bond’s 10-year lifespan. The District structured that bond in 
a way that did not raise property tax rates, but keeping the bond tax-neutral also meant it 
wouldn’t cover everything the District knew it needed.  The Board of Education hoped state 
funding would increase sufficiently when the economy got better, but that hasn’t happened.  
• As a result, the District continues to struggle to pay for important things like preventative 
maintenance on its buildings.
• Recent legislative adjustments to appropriate uses for a sinking fund have now made this a 
potential avenue for covering some significant district costs, such as maintenance, facility 
improvements and construction, safety and security measures, and technology. 
32017 Sinking Fund Community Input Survey Report472
Survey Background
• Consequently, the Troy Board of Education is considering whether or not to place a sinking fund 
proposal on the election ballot this November.  
• The District recently retired some debt, so it could structure a new 1-mill sinking fund so that 
the total school millage rate in Troy would stay where it is, with no property tax increase from 
what homeowners pay today.  That 1-mill would provide the District with 3.6 million dollars per 
year for the next ten years.  The funds would be used to fill current holes in preventative 
maintenance, update classrooms and technology in a timelier manner, and cover any debt 
payments on new or existing buildings.
• Given ongoing needs, it would be appropriate for the district to ask for more than 1-mill—
especially because a school district can only pursue one sinking fund every ten years.
• As a result, the Board commissioned a public survey of stakeholders across the Troy community 
to determine the electorate’s willingness to support this form of funding the district.
42017 Sinking Fund Community Input Survey Report473
Methodology and Sample
Methodology
• Phone survey fielded by Epic MRA, a 
Lansing-based market research 
company (firm that completed the 
2013 TSD Bond survey).
• Average of 18 minutes in length.
• Fielded 4/20 to 4/24/17.
• To keep District costs as low as 
possible, a Board member with 
market research expertise drafted 
and analyzed the survey following 
standard research industry practices.
Sample
• 400 Troy residents who live within the Troy School 
District area.
• Registered voters who indicate they are at least 
“seldom” voters in local school related elections.
• Age distribution consistent with voting patterns 
from ’11 and ’13 Troy elections.
• 20% of interviews were completed with cell-only 
households.
• Cooperation rate was extremely high: 80% of those 
who answered and qualified completed the survey.
